narrative.summary: Madagascar has no AI-specific law, strategy or guidance. Its only AI-relevant binding rules are in the 2015 personal data protection law (Law 2014-038), which bars court decisions based on automated profiling and decisions based solely on it, and gives people the right to know the logic of automated decisions with legal effects; the data protection commission (CMIL) that enforces it was organised by a 2023 decree. The digital ministry mentions AI ambitions only in news posts.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Digital Development, Posts and Telecommunications
Commission Malagasy sur l'Informatique et des Libertés (CMIL)
narrative.review_notes: A follow-up review on 18 October 2026 searched the national legislation portal, the digital ministry's laws and decrees pages, the National Assembly and Senate, the standards bureau and the procurement regulator, and found no new AI material. The data protection commission's and telecom regulator's websites still could not be accessed and the central bank's site was unavailable; the national cybersecurity strategy and the 2023-2028 digital strategic plan are held as leads until their texts are published.

instruments.summary: Madagascar's general data protection law, covering any automated or non-automated processing of personal data on Malagasy territory, and creating the Commission Malagasy de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CMIL) as independent supervisory authority with regulatory and sanctioning powers. Article 3 bars court decisions assessing human behaviour from being based on automated profiling and bars administrative or private decisions from being based solely on such processing; data subjects may obtain information to understand and contest the logic of automated processing behind decisions with legal effects. Automated processing on behalf of the State and public bodies requires a regulatory act after a reasoned opinion of the CMIL.
instruments.current_status: Promulgated in Antananarivo on 9 January 2015 after adoption by the National Assembly on 16 December 2014 and High Constitutional Court decision no. 02-HCC/D3 of 7 January 2015. The national legislation portal (CNLEGIS) lists it as in force, published in Journal Officiel no. 3630 of 20 July 2015, p. 3272, and links Decree no. 2023-1541 as its implementing decree. CMIL members were designated by Decree no. 2025-814 of 30 July 2025 (located on the portal).

instruments.summary: Implementing decree of Law No. 2014-038 that sets up the CMIL as the independent administrative authority for personal data protection, listing its powers (recommendations, individual and regulatory decisions, simplified norms, on-site and online inspections, sanctions, labels) and its duty to monitor information-technology developments and report on their effects on privacy. It sets the nine-member deliberative body, the executive secretariat and directorates (rights protection, compliance, communication, information systems) and the CMIL's budget rules.
instruments.current_status: Signed in Antananarivo on 6 December 2023; Journal Officiel no. 4195 of 8 April 2024, p. 1138 (per CNLEGIS record); entered into force immediately on broadcast publication (Art. 91). Decree no. 2025-696 of 18 June 2025 repealed only its Article 90 (transitional status as a public administrative body). The CNLEGIS record nevertheless labels the decree 'Abrogé'; the primary text of Decree 2025-696 repeals only Article 90, so it is recorded as in force.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Madagascar's national legislation portal, the National Assembly, the digital ministry, other ministries and regulators were searched in French. Only the data protection law and its implementing decree were found; no AI law, national AI strategy, AI policy or public-sector AI guidance has been published, and no AI material was found in any other category. The data protection authority's and the telecoms regulator's websites were unavailable and the national cybersecurity strategy text is not online, so these remain to be checked.
